subject: MSA & Order Form — proposed carve-out language for confidentiality / trade secrets
body:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbledata.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@nimbledata.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Oct 2025 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines — confidentiality / liability carve-outs

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Our procurement team reviewed and pushed back primarily on the limitation of liability section. They want an explicit carve-out so any breach of confidentiality (including accidental exposure) and misappropriation of trade secrets are excluded from the cap.

We appreciate Redwood's position on overall caps, but our legal counsel is insisting on stronger protection for our IP and customer data. I've attached our redline (Nimble_MSA_redline_v3.docx) with comments. Can we set up a quick sync between legal teams to see if there's middle ground?

Best,
Alex Morgan
Director, Business Operations
NimbleData Inc.

---

On Fri, 24 Oct 2025 at 11:05 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbledata.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — confidentiality / liability carve-outs

Alex — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're open to discussing confidentiality carve-outs, but we need to balance exposure across the contract (our order sizes and the hosting model matter).

Next steps:
- I'll loop in our legal lead Jonas to handle specific language.
- Can you confirm whether NimbleData is asking that all confidentiality breaches be entirely uncapped, or only those that rise to the level of misappropriation of trade secrets and willful breaches?
- Propose a 30‑minute call next week; I'll send a calendar invite once we have availability.

Attachment(s): —
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Fri, 24 Oct 2025 at 12:18 PM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbledata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Oct 2025 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — confidentiality / liability carve-outs

Alex / Rachel,

Thanks — quick read-through here. We're generally comfortable carving confidentiality breaches out of the monetary cap where there's actual unauthorized access to NimbleData's trade secrets or personal data, but we need to narrow definitions to avoid an uncapped, open-ended exposure for minor procedural slip-ups. A few items we suggest:

1) Define "Confidential Information" and explicitly identify "Trade Secrets" per the Uniform Trade Secrets Act (or equivalent), and require that claimants notify Redwood and provide a forensic report showing misappropriation.

2) Limit uncapped liability to willful misconduct or gross negligence that resulted in the disclosure of trade secrets or regulated personal data.

3) For other confidentiality breaches (e.g., inadvertent access or temporary misconfiguration), propose a separate sub-cap (e.g., 200% of fees paid in prior 12 months OR $2M, whichever is greater).

4) Consider requiring commercially reasonable mitigation steps and cooperation on remediation before uncapped damages apply.

If NimbleData insists on a broader uncapped carve-out, we will need to escalate to commercial leadership for pricing and insurance changes. Happy to discuss on a call.

-Jonas
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference

---

On Mon, 27 Oct 2025 at 09:03 AM Dana Liu <dana.liu@bryantlaw.com> wrote:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@bryantlaw.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbledata.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — confidentiality / liability carve-outs

Jonas, Rachel — representing NimbleData on this matter. Nimble's position is:

- A total carve-out from the liability cap for any breach of confidentiality or misappropriation of trade secrets. They are unwilling to accept a monetary sub-cap for those categories.
- They are amenable to process safeguards (notification, preservation of evidence), but not to having to prove willful misconduct as a precondition to uncapped recovery.

We understand Redwood's exposure concerns. Please advise whether Redwood can accept an uncapped carve-out limited to cases where (i) trade secrets are proven to have been misappropriated, or (ii) there is unauthorized access to regulated personal data that causes material regulatory liability to Nimble. If you can accept those two narrow buckets without a willfulness threshold, we can try to craft language that contains sufficient procedural protections.

Thanks,
Dana Liu
Partner, Bryant & Co. LLP

---

On Mon, 27 Oct 2025 at 11:10 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@bryantlaw.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbledata.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — confidentiality / liability carve-outs

Dana — thanks for the clarity.

Jonas and I discussed internally. High level: we can consider an uncapped carve-out that is limited to proven misappropriation of trade secrets and unauthorized access to regulated personal data that triggers NimbleData's regulatory liability, but Redwood needs:

- Clear, objective standards for establishing "misappropriation" (forensic report; reasonable evidentiary threshold).
- A cure/remediation period and opportunity to contest findings (e.g., independent expert review if disputed).
- Insurance / indemnity language to the extent an uncapped exposure is accepted — we need to confirm limits with Finance.

Karthik — FYI this may impact deal economics; if Nimble stands firm on a fully uncapped position without a willfulness or sub-cap for less severe breaches, we should consider either adding a contractual insurance requirement or revisiting pricing/commitments.

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

On Thu, 30 Oct 2025 at 16:12:00 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@bryantlaw.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbledata.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — confidentiality / liability carve-outs

Team — after reviewing the commercial impact, here's a pragmatic proposal to present to NimbleData:

1) Carve-out (uncapped) will apply only to: (a) proven misappropriation of trade secrets (as defined and evidenced by a forensic report and/or court order); and (b) unauthorized access to regulated personal data that results in material regulatory fines or obligations to NimbleData.

2) For all other confidentiality breaches (including inadvertent disclosure, misrouting of email, or temporary configuration errors), apply a sub-cap equal to the greater of (i) 200% of Redwood fees paid by NimbleData in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $2,000,000.

3) Require a mandatory, good-faith dispute escalation process: independent expert review if parties cannot agree on whether the incident meets the misappropriation threshold. Costs of the independent review to be borne by the non-prevailing party.

4) Redwood to provide evidence of current cyber insurance and to extend notice to Nimble within 48 hours of any suspected incident.

If NimbleData can accept those guardrails in writing, we can sign the MSA and proceed with the Order Form. If not, we'll need to present the counterparty options (higher pricing, minimum commitment, or additional insurance requirements).

Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

---

Next steps (internal):
- Rachel to send Karthik/Jonas a short doc summarizing the proposed language for legal approval and to share our insurance certificate.
- Schedule a 30-minute call with NimbleData (Dana/Alex) to review the proposal and confirm whether the sub-cap meets their risk tolerance.
- HubSpot note: HS-3421 updated with these terms and attachments.
